title: Fact-check of the 'caveman' Claude Code skill: claimed 65% token cut, measured ~30% fewer output tokens on two tasks

tools.name: caveman (skill/plugin)
tools.detail: free plugin/skill that makes Claude respond tersely to cut output tokens; source repo shown only as a thumbnail with 13,515 (stars?)

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.detail: usage panel shows 5-hour limit and weekly limits, 'This session' cost/API time/active time/cache hit, breakdown Opus 5 input/output/cache tokens

claims: Claim under test: caveman cuts tokens Claude spends by ~65%
Test 1 (explain an algorithm): 4,000 output tokens without caveman vs 2,800 with = ~30% decrease
Test 2 (implement an FAQ page): 4,900 vs 2,400 output tokens = ~30% decrease (closer to 50% by the numbers quoted)
Output quality 'pretty much the same', structure tighter with less waffle
how_to_steps: Install the caveman skill in Claude Code
Run the same prompt with and without the skill
Compare output tokens in the Claude Code usage panel (/usage or /cost)
on_screen_only: 'Fact or Hype?' card; FACT / HYPE checkboxes

relevance.why: Token limits on Max are a daily constraint; an empirically tested ~30% output reduction with no quality loss is a cheap win, and the test method (same prompt, compare usage) is itself a good habit.

implement_score.why: Install caveman (or an equivalent terse-output instruction in CLAUDE.md) and A/B it on real tasks. Note the saving is on output tokens only, which are a minority of most sessions' spend; input/cache dominates.

verify: Exact repo for 'caveman' (owner, stars) and whether it is a skill, plugin or output style
